summary.name: Frink
summary.one_liner: Frink is a desktop-first, open-source (MIT) app for running parallel AI coding agents and multi-step workflows triggered by schedules, webhooks, or events from tools like Linear and Sentry.
use_cases: running several coding agents in parallel
automating tasks triggered by new Linear tickets
reacting to Sentry errors with an agent workflow
reviewing agent file diffs and fixing lines
adding approval gates to automated runs
summary.what_it_does: Frink lets you run multiple AI agents side by side, with up to four agents each in their own git worktree while a Flow runs in the background. Flows (workflows) can be started by hand, on a schedule, from a connected tool, or when a task completes. Flows support conditions that choose between two paths and approval steps that pause a run until you decide. You can describe a custom step in chat and the agent writes it, including inputs and outputs, and it then appears in the step picker. Connected tools add their actions as steps, and each step can use the output of the previous one. The page also mentions an editor, debug mode, and importing your existing tool setup.
notable: Runs multiple coding agents in parallel in their own git worktrees
Workflows triggered by schedules, webhooks, or Linear/Sentry events
Agent can write new custom workflow steps from a chat request
caveats: Listed as Early Access on the page
Platforms named are macOS and Linux only; no Windows mentioned
Up to four agents running in parallel
